title: Unchecked Null Pointers from FFI Calls
pattern: Directly dereferencing a raw pointer returned by an external C library or FFI function without performing a null check.
why_bad: C libraries commonly return NULL on allocation or connection failure. Directly dereferencing a NULL pointer leads to immediate segment faults or undefined behavior.
detection: Dereferencing a pointer returned from an `extern "C"` block inside an unsafe block without checking `ptr.is_null()` first.
counterexample: Checking nullness and converting to a safe Rust Option: `Option::from_raw`.
fix: Check for nullness before dereferencing: `if conn.is_null() { return Err(Error::NullPointer); }`.
source: Steve McConnell, Code Complete (Checklist: Data Declarations) [549, 571].
